title: Kioxia unveils E1.L SSDs for hyperscalers with up to 122.88TB capacity — extreme density meets compact form factor
key_facts: Kioxia introduced its LD4-series SSDs in the E1.L form factor with capacities up to 122.88TB for hyperscale data centres, on Friday 9 Oct 2026.
The drives use BiCS8 3D QLC NAND and target read-intensive workloads such as AI data repositories and object storage.
The company currently offers up to 30.72TB and has validated an architecture for 122.88TB, with no availability date.
Kioxia is sampling 15.36TB and 30.72TB drives to select customers.
Kioxia did not disclose sequential speeds, IOPS, latency, endurance or power consumption.
The drives list PCIe 5.0 compliance but operate at PCIe 4.0 x4 speeds.
They will be demonstrated at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose in mid-October.
quote_evidence: Kioxia introduced its LD4-series solid-state drives (SSDs) in an E1.L form factor with capacities up to 122.88TB designed for high-density storage deployments in hyperscale data centers on Friday.
The company has not disclosed when 122.88 TB configurations will become available or when the series will enter mass production.
Interestingly, Kioxia did not disclose any actual performance characteristics of its LD4-series SSDs, including sequential read and write speeds, random read and write IOPS, or latency.
why_it_matters_hint: More storage per thin server matters for AI data, but the biggest drive is undated and unmeasured.
